title: Indian Embassy in UAE Warns Against Agencies Promising Jobs and Residency Visas
excerpt: Missions in Abu Dhabi and Dubai say agencies advertising third-country jobs and residency on social media collect fees and deliver nothing, and that no agency can guarantee a visa.
body:
• The Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General in Dubai warned on October 12 against agencies that collect fees for third-country jobs and residency visas, then deliver nothing and refund nothing.
  • No private agency can guarantee a visa — only the issuing government decides, the missions said.
  • Action step: verify any offer with the destination country's embassy, and contact the Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra on toll-free 80046342 before paying anyone.
  • An earlier August advisory warned that biometric data shared with unauthorised agents can be misused to open bank accounts and take loans in a victim's name.

Indian missions in the UAE have warned Indian nationals against fraudulent visa and migration agencies that advertise third-country employment and residency services on social media, collect fees, and then fail to deliver the service or return the money.

In an advisory dated October 12, the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Northern Emirates said they had received complaints against agencies operating outside India, including in the UAE. The missions urged Indians not to rely solely on online advertisements or to trust private visa processing agencies, particularly those based outside India.

"Never pay any amount based on promises of visa approval."

— Embassy of India, Abu Dhabi, and Consulate General of India, Dubai

How the Pitch Works

The pattern described by the missions is consistent. An agency promotes employment or residency in a third country through social media, presents itself as able to secure the visa, and collects payment up front. The promised service does not arrive, and neither does a refund.

https://x.com/TeamNewsfy/status/2111070782503981477

The missions' core point is structural, not just cautionary: visa approval is solely the decision of the government issuing the visa. An intermediary can submit paperwork, but it cannot sell an outcome it does not control. Any fee charged against a guarantee of approval is, by that test alone, a warning sign. Applicants were advised to verify visa requirements, procedures and authorised channels directly with the embassy or consulate of the destination country in their country of residence, and to use official government and embassy websites for current information, as reported by The Times of India and Curly Tales.

The Earlier Warning: Your Biometrics Are the Prize

The October advisory follows an August 24 warning about a more damaging variant. In that notice, the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi said unauthorised individuals offering help with visa regularisation, emergency certificates, exit permits, Emirates IDs and employment procedures were collecting personal documents and biometric information. That data, the embassy said, could be misused to open bank accounts, obtain loans and take credit cards without the victim's knowledge, leaving the victim liable for transactions they never made.

The embassy directed Indians seeking assistance to the Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra, and said biometric information required for official procedures should be provided only at authorised UAE government facilities.

What to Do Before You Pay Anyone

Start with the destination, not the agent. Check the requirements and authorised channels on the official site of the country you want to move to, in your country of residence. If an agency's claim differs from that page, the page governs.

If you need help verifying an agency or an offer, contact the Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra before money or documents change hands. And treat two requests as automatic refusals: payment in exchange for guaranteed approval, and passport, Emirates ID or biometric details handed to a private intermediary.

What Comes Next

The missions have urged Indian nationals in the UAE to verify immigration claims through official channels and to exercise caution before paying agents or sharing sensitive personal information. Complaints are what produced both the August and October advisories, so reporting a suspicious agency to the embassy or consulate is the mechanism that triggers the next warning.
